newsitem.title: UK: UK animal welfare group welcomes EU transport move.
newsitem.headline: UK animal welfare group welcomes EU transport move.

text.p: An EU Commission decision to propose a link between animal welfare and the payment of European Union beef export subsidies was welcomed by campaigners on Wednesday.
"We think it is a great leap forward," a spokesman for Britain's Royal Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals said. But he added that the society's long term aim was an end to live exports.
"What we're trying to do is to make sure that it's uneconomic to export live beef to third countries," he said. The RSPCA wanted export subsidies phased out.
Under the Uruguay Round trade deal that would eventually happen, he said, and there had already been some reductions by the EU.
But the spokesman said that at present "the exporter gets the subsidy as long as the animal arrives alive. There's no compassionate consideration as long as it arrives alive."

The Commission proposal, which is subject to the approval of EU farm ministers, follows pressure from Sweden and other northern EU member states after reports of unacceptable suffering by farm animals being transported long distances.

The Commission has proposed amending the EU regulations governing the beef sector to add the words, "...the payment of the refund for exports of live animals is subject to...the protection of animals during transport."
Detailed implementing rules would be defined by the EU's beef management committee, a group of officials from the individual countries which meets regularly in Brussels.
